learn.rule: A summary is one sentence. It tells who or what the text is about and the most important thing. Leave out tiny details and your opinions.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una sola oración. Dice de quién o de qué trata el texto y lo más importante. Deja fuera los detalles pequeños y tus opiniones.
learn.model: Frogs grow from eggs into tadpoles and then into adult frogs.
learn.notice: The sentence names who it is about, frogs, and the most important thing, how they change.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of this passage?
items.text: Honeybees cannot talk, but they can still share news. When a bee finds good flowers, she returns to the hive and does a waggle dance. The angle of her dance shows other bees which way to fly. Worker bees are about half an inch long, and a hive may hold 50,000 bees.

options.text: Honeybees dance.
Honeybees do a waggle dance to show other bees where to find flowers.
Honeybees, which are about half an inch long and live in hives of up to 50,000 bees, do a waggle dance to show other bees which way to fly.

items.why: A summary names the topic and the key idea in one sentence. Choice A is too short to be useful, and choice C is packed with tiny details.
items.whyEs: Un resumen nombra el tema y la idea clave en una oración. La opción A es demasiado corta y la opción C está llena de detalles pequeños.

items.prompt: Check the details you should cut from a one-sentence summary of the bee passage.
items.text: Honeybees cannot talk, but they can still share news. When a bee finds good flowers, she returns to the hive and does a waggle dance. The angle of her dance shows other bees which way to fly. Worker bees are about half an inch long, and a hive may hold 50,000 bees.

options.text: A bee that finds flowers does a waggle dance.
Worker bees are about half an inch long.
The dance shows other bees which way to fly.
A hive may hold 50,000 bees.

items.why: A summary keeps the main idea: the dance and what it tells. The size of a bee and the number of bees in a hive are small facts that you can cut.
items.whyEs: Un resumen conserva la idea principal: el baile y lo que dice. El tamaño de una abeja y el número de abejas en una colmena son datos pequeños que puedes quitar.

items.prompt: Complete the summary frame with the most important words.
items.text: Honeybees cannot talk, but they can still share news. When a bee finds good flowers, she returns to the hive and does a waggle dance. The angle of her dance shows other bees which way to fly.
parts: A honeybee that finds flowers does a
items.model: A honeybee that finds flowers does a waggle dance to show other bees which way to fly.
items.why: The frame needs the main action, the waggle dance, and why it matters, showing which way to fly. Those are the two key ideas of the passage.
items.whyEs: El esquema necesita la acción principal, el baile, y por qué importa: mostrar hacia dónde volar. Esas son las dos ideas clave del pasaje.

items.prompt: Which summary has the wrong focus?
items.text: Honeybees cannot talk, but they can still share news. When a bee finds good flowers, she returns to the hive and does a waggle dance. The angle of her dance shows other bees which way to fly. Worker bees are about half an inch long, and a hive may hold 50,000 bees.

options.text: Worker honeybees are tiny insects that live in large hives.
Honeybees use a dance to share where food is.
Honeybees show other bees which way to fly by dancing.

items.why: Choice A focuses on the size and home of the bees, which are small details. Choices B and C both tell the most important idea, the dance.
items.whyEs: La opción A se centra en el tamaño y el hogar de las abejas, que son detalles pequeños. Las opciones B y C dicen la idea más importante: el baile.

items.prompt: Read the new passage. Which sentence is the best summary?
items.text: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky. Inside storm clouds, tiny bits of ice bump together and build up electric charge. When the charge gets strong enough, it jumps to the ground or to another cloud. The flash heats the air so fast that the air booms, which we hear as thunder.

options.text: Lightning is the most exciting part of a storm.
Tiny bits of ice bump together, build up charge, and jump to the ground, and then the hot air booms as thunder.
Lightning is a huge spark of electricity that forms in storm clouds.

items.why: A good summary tells what the passage is about and its main point. Choice A is an opinion, and choice B retells every step instead of summarizing.
items.whyEs: Un buen resumen dice de qué trata el pasaje y su punto principal. La opción A es una opinión y la opción B cuenta cada paso en lugar de resumir.

items.prompt: Which summary of the lightning passage is too short to be helpful?
items.text: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky. Inside storm clouds, tiny bits of ice bump together and build up electric charge. When the charge gets strong enough, it jumps to the ground or to another cloud. The flash heats the air so fast that the air booms, which we hear as thunder.

options.text: Lightning happens.
A storm cloud builds up electric charge, and when it jumps, we see lightning and hear thunder.
Lightning is an electric spark from storm clouds that makes the air boom.

items.why: Choice A names the topic but says nothing important about it. A summary needs the topic and the key point together.
items.whyEs: La opción A nombra el tema, pero no dice nada importante sobre él. Un resumen necesita el tema y el punto clave juntos.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the passage. Tell who it is about and the most important thing.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el pasaje. Di de quién trata y lo más importante.
write.text: Sea otters live along the Pacific coast. They float on their backs and eat shellfish such as crabs and clams. To crack open a hard shell, an otter places a rock on its chest and hits the shell against it. Otters even hold hands while they sleep so they do not drift apart.

label: I named who it is about
Nombré de quién trata

write.model: Sea otters use rocks as tools to crack open the shells of the shellfish they eat.

familyTalk.en: After a show or a story, each person gives a one-sentence summary. Compare which one has the most important idea.
familyTalk.es: Después de un programa o un cuento, cada persona da un resumen de una oración. Comparen cuál tiene la idea más importante.

teacherTip.en: Have students cross out tiny details in the passage with a pencil first. What is left is the summary.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes tachen primero los detalles pequeños del pasaje con un lápiz. Lo que queda es el resumen.

learn.rule: Find who or what the text is about. Then find the most important thing. Put both in one sentence and leave the extras out.
learn.ruleEs: Busca de quién o de qué trata el texto. Luego busca lo más importante. Pon ambas cosas en una oración y deja fuera lo extra.
learn.model: Libraries lend books and offer programs that help a whole community learn.
learn.notice: The sentence names libraries and the most important thing they do. It leaves out the names of specific books.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of this passage?
items.text: Before 1825, moving goods from the Atlantic coast to the Great Lakes was slow and costly. New York built the Erie Canal, a waterway about 363 miles long that linked the Hudson River to Lake Erie. Mules walked along the bank and pulled the boats. Shipping a ton of goods dropped from about 100 dollars to about 10 dollars, and cities such as Buffalo and Rochester grew quickly.

options.text: The canal was long.
The Erie Canal, about 363 miles long, used mules to cut shipping costs from 100 dollars to 10 dollars and helped Buffalo and Rochester grow.
The Erie Canal made shipping goods across New York faster and cheaper.

items.why: The best summary names the canal and its biggest effect. Choice A is too short, and choice B squeezes in too many numbers and names.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen nombra el canal y su efecto más importante. La opción A es demasiado corta y la B mete demasiados números y nombres.

items.prompt: Check the details you should cut from a one-sentence summary of the canal passage.
items.text: Before 1825, moving goods from the Atlantic coast to the Great Lakes was slow and costly. New York built the Erie Canal, a waterway about 363 miles long that linked the Hudson River to Lake Erie. Mules walked along the bank and pulled the boats. Shipping a ton of goods dropped from about 100 dollars to about 10 dollars, and cities such as Buffalo and Rochester grew quickly.

options.text: Mules walked along the bank and pulled the boats.
Shipping goods became much cheaper.
The canal linked the Hudson River to Lake Erie.
The canal was about 363 miles long.

items.why: The cheaper shipping and the link between the river and the lake are the heart of the passage. How mules pulled boats and the exact length are smaller details.
items.whyEs: El envío más barato y la unión entre el río y el lago son el corazón del pasaje. Cómo las mulas jalaban los botes y la longitud exacta son detalles menores.

items.text: Before 1825, moving goods from the Atlantic coast to the Great Lakes was slow and costly. New York built the Erie Canal, a waterway about 363 miles long that linked the Hudson River to Lake Erie. Shipping a ton of goods dropped from about 100 dollars to about 10 dollars.
items.model: New York built the Erie Canal so goods could travel faster and for less money.
items.why: The two blanks hold the who or what, the Erie Canal, and the key result, faster and cheaper travel for goods. Nothing else is needed.
items.whyEs: Los dos espacios contienen el qué, el Canal Erie, y el resultado clave: viajes más rápidos y baratos para las mercancías. No se necesita nada más.

items.prompt: Which summary of the canal passage has the wrong focus?
items.text: Before 1825, moving goods from the Atlantic coast to the Great Lakes was slow and costly. New York built the Erie Canal, a waterway about 363 miles long that linked the Hudson River to Lake Erie. Mules walked along the bank and pulled the boats. Shipping a ton of goods dropped from about 100 dollars to about 10 dollars, and cities such as Buffalo and Rochester grew quickly.

options.text: Mules walked beside the boats on the Erie Canal.
New York built a canal to move goods across the state.
The Erie Canal made shipping cheaper and faster.

items.why: Choice A is about the mules, which is only one small detail. Choices B and C both tell the main idea of the whole passage.
items.whyEs: La opción A trata de las mulas, que son solo un detalle pequeño. Las opciones B y C dicen la idea principal de todo el pasaje.

items.prompt: Read the new passage. Which sentence is the best summary?
items.text: Communities need rules. A rule at a pool says no running, so people do not slip and get hurt. A rule at a library asks people to speak softly, so everyone can read in peace. A rule on a road says to stop at a red light, so drivers and walkers stay safe.

options.text: A rule at a library asks people to speak softly so everyone can read.
Rules in a community keep people safe and help everyone share places.
A pool has a rule about running, a library has a rule about talking, and a road has a rule about red lights.

items.why: A summary gives the main idea of all the examples. Choice A uses only one example, and choice C is a list of every example.
items.whyEs: Un resumen da la idea principal de todos los ejemplos. La opción A usa solo un ejemplo y la opción C es una lista de todos los ejemplos.

items.prompt: Which summary of the rules passage is too short to tell the main idea?
items.text: Communities need rules. A rule at a pool says no running, so people do not slip and get hurt. A rule at a library asks people to speak softly, so everyone can read in peace. A rule on a road says to stop at a red light, so drivers and walkers stay safe.

options.text: Communities have rules.
Rules keep people safe and help everyone enjoy shared places.
Rules at pools, libraries, and roads keep people safe and comfortable.

items.why: Choice A says rules exist, but not why they matter. A strong summary also tells the most important idea about the topic.
items.whyEs: La opción A dice que existen reglas, pero no por qué importan. Un buen resumen también dice la idea más importante sobre el tema.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the passage. Tell who or what it is about and the most important thing.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el pasaje. Di de quién o de qué trata y lo más importante.
write.text: A compass is a tool that helps people find direction. Inside it is a small magnetic needle that always points toward Earth's magnetic north. Hikers and sailors use compasses so they do not get lost. Long ago, travelers used the stars for the same purpose.

label: I named what it is about
Nombré de qué trata

write.model: A compass has a magnetic needle that points north and helps travelers find their way.

familyTalk.en: Read a short news story together. Each person says what it was about and the most important thing in one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Lean juntos una noticia corta. Cada persona dice de qué trataba y lo más importante en una oración.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to count the details in a wrong summary. A too-long summary usually has three or more.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes cuenten los detalles de un resumen incorrecto. Un resumen demasiado largo suele tener tres o más.

learn.rule: To summarize a story, tell who the story is about and what mainly happens. Skip small details such as colors and clothes.
learn.ruleEs: Para resumir un cuento, di de quién trata y qué ocurre principalmente. Omite los detalles pequeños, como los colores y la ropa.
learn.model: Jin found a lost kitten and brought it back to its owner.
learn.notice: The sentence names the character and the main event. It does not say what Jin wore or what color the kitten was.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of this story?
items.text: Mei wore her favorite green boots to the school garden. One tomato plant was drooping, and the soil around it was dry. Mei asked her classmates to take turns watering it each morning. A few weeks later, the plant stood tall, and the class shared its six red tomatoes.

options.text: Mei wore green boots to the school garden.
Mei wore green boots, saw a dry plant, asked classmates to water it, and later shared six tomatoes.
Mei's class saved a drooping tomato plant by taking turns watering it.

items.why: A story summary tells who and the main event. Choice A is a small detail, and choice B lists too many small events.
items.whyEs: El resumen de un cuento dice quién y el suceso principal. La opción A es un detalle pequeño y la opción B enumera demasiados sucesos pequeños.

items.prompt: Check the details you should cut from a one-sentence summary of Mei's story.
items.text: Mei wore her favorite green boots to the school garden. One tomato plant was drooping, and the soil around it was dry. Mei asked her classmates to take turns watering it each morning. A few weeks later, the plant stood tall, and the class shared its six red tomatoes.

options.text: Mei wore her favorite green boots.
Classmates took turns watering the plant.
The plant was drooping and the soil was dry.
The plant grew six red tomatoes.

items.why: The problem, the plant was drooping, and the solution, taking turns watering, are the story's main events. The boots and the number of tomatoes are small details.
items.whyEs: El problema, la planta caída, y la solución, turnarse para regarla, son los sucesos principales del cuento. Las botas y el número de tomates son detalles pequeños.

items.prompt: Complete the summary frame with the most important action.
items.text: Mei asked her classmates to take turns watering the plant each morning. A few weeks later, the plant stood tall.
parts: Mei's class saved the drooping tomato plant by

options: moving it to a sunnier spot

items.model: Mei's class saved the drooping tomato plant by taking turns watering it each morning.
items.why: The blank holds the main action that solved the problem. The story says classmates watered the plant, not that they bought a pot or moved it.
items.whyEs: El espacio contiene la acción principal que resolvió el problema. El cuento dice que los compañeros regaron la planta, no que compraron una maceta ni que la movieron.

items.prompt: Which summary of Mei's story has the wrong focus?
items.text: Mei wore her favorite green boots to the school garden. One tomato plant was drooping, and the soil around it was dry. Mei asked her classmates to take turns watering it each morning. A few weeks later, the plant stood tall, and the class shared its six red tomatoes.

options.text: A class worked together to help a plant grow strong.
Mei and her classmates solved a plant's problem with teamwork.
Mei has a favorite pair of boots.

items.why: Choice C is about the boots, which is not the main point of the story. Choices A and B both tell what mainly happens.
items.whyEs: La opción C trata de las botas, que no son el punto principal del cuento. Las opciones A y B dicen lo que ocurre principalmente.

items.prompt: Read the new story. Which sentence is the best summary?
items.text: Omar loved to draw, but he never showed anyone his sketches. One day his teacher found a drawing of the school's old oak tree on the floor. She hung it in the hallway, and classmates stopped to admire it. Omar smiled and began to share his sketchbook.

options.text: Omar became willing to share his drawings after his teacher displayed one.
The school has an old oak tree.
Omar loved to draw, his teacher found a drawing of the oak tree on the floor, she hung it in the hallway, and then Omar shared his sketchbook.

items.why: The best summary tells the character and the change in the story. Choice B is a small detail, and choice C retells every event.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen dice el personaje y el cambio en el cuento. La opción B es un detalle pequeño y la opción C vuelve a contar todos los sucesos.

items.prompt: Which summary of Omar's story is too short to be helpful?
items.text: Omar loved to draw, but he never showed anyone his sketches. One day his teacher found a drawing of the school's old oak tree on the floor. She hung it in the hallway, and classmates stopped to admire it. Omar smiled and began to share his sketchbook.

options.text: A teacher helped a shy artist feel proud of his drawings.
Omar draws.
Omar began sharing his drawings after classmates admired one in the hallway.

items.why: Choice B tells who the story is about but leaves out what happens. A good summary needs the main event too.
items.whyEs: La opción B dice de quién trata el cuento, pero omite lo que ocurre. Un buen resumen también necesita el suceso principal.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the passage. Tell who or what it is about and the most important thing.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el pasaje. Di de quién o de qué trata y lo más importante.
write.text: Drums are some of the oldest instruments. People strike a drum to make a beat, and the sound changes with the size of the drum. A small drum sounds high, and a large drum sounds low. Drummers around the world use rhythms to tell stories and to bring people together.

label: I named what it is about
Nombré de qué trata

write.model: Drums make beats that change with their size and help people tell stories and come together.

familyTalk.en: After a favorite movie, each person gives a one-sentence summary. Check that it names the character and the main event.
familyTalk.es: Después de una película favorita, cada persona da un resumen de una oración. Revisen que nombre al personaje y el suceso principal.

teacherTip.en: Use a who-did-what frame on the board and ask students to fill it from a story before they write freely.
teacherTip.es: Usa en la pizarra un esquema de quién hizo qué y pide que los estudiantes lo llenen con un cuento antes de escribir con libertad.
